statutes.act: Read With Section 149 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The appellants are five in number and they have filed this appeal as of right. They were acquitted by the trial court but convicted by the High Court on appeal filed by the State, under Section 302, Section 325 read with Section 149 of the Indian Penal Code besides the offence of rioting under Section 148 of the Indian Penal Code.

All the five accused formed themselves into an unlawful assembly on the evening of 24-10-1985 and lay in ambush waiting for Bahadur Singh (deceased) to come through the road and on seeing Bahadur Singh they all launched an attack with weapons like gandasa, takua and ghope.

The wife of Bahadur Singh (Ranjit Kaur, PW 10) who accompanied her husband made a bid to rescue her husband from the onslaughts of the assailants, but she too was attacked by them. Bahadur Singh died at the spot.

Subsequently all the five accused were arrested and on the strength of the information elicited from Ist accused Chet Singh and third accused Ginder Singh weapons of offences were recovered from concealed places.

The most important witness in this case is PW 10 (Ranjit Kaur). The importance of her evidence is that no court can possibly hold that she would not have witnessed the occurrence, for she herself sustained as many as eight injuries, some of them serious, during the occurrence.
petitioner_arguments: The defence version was that PW 10 would have possibly sustained those injuries at some other place and at some other time and not when she was accompanying her husband at the place of occurrence.
That suggestion is too unconvincing and very far-fetched. No court can give any weight to such a theory.
court_reasoning: The fact that PW 10 has so many injuries would probabilise her version that when she found her husband in great danger being attacked by the assailants she threw herself into a vortex for rescuing the father of all her little children from being killed like that.
That accounts for the large number of injuries which she sustained at the spot itself.
We are confident that PW 10 (Ranjit Kaur) was a witness to the occurrence and if so she was able to see the assailants whose identity she knew even earlier.
holding: We direct the appellants to surrender to the bail. We also direct the Sessions Judge, Sangrur to take prompt steps to put the appellants back in jail to serve the remaining period of sentence.
